Addresses genuine practical limitations: few-step generation (8 steps without distillation), audio conditioning, and long-form synthesis
Comprehensive evaluation with multiple complementary metrics, blind human evaluation (18 participants), and test set up to 30 seconds
Novel application of shortcut loss to V2A generation domain (first in field), enabling efficient sampling without post-training distillation
Effective system design combining masked flow matching, shortcut loss, and contrastively-trained synchronization model
Practical capabilities demonstrated: audio conditioning preserves spectral characteristics (SWSD metric), long-form generation maintains quality over extended durations
Thorough presentation with clear methodology, comprehensive related work, detailed implementation details (A.4-A.5), and informative visualizations

Incomplete ablation studies: no isolation of new synchronization model impact versus Synchformer, missing ablation on masked training objective alone, no component-wise contribution analysis

Long-form comparison potentially confounded: SALSA-V generates iteratively (forced 10s context with 0.5s prepend) while MMAudio processes full sequence, and comparison shows MMAudio advantages up to 20s where it has full context access
Audio fidelity gap not fully explored: 2.96 vs 3.16 MOS for audio fidelity (SALSA-V lower), attributed to 643M vs 1.03B parameters but no investigation of architectural contributions to tradeoff

Limited human evaluation scope: only 10 videos and 18 participants for synchronization claims, no human evaluation of long-form consistency or scene transition handling despite acknowledged limitations
Synchronization metric limitations: DeSync resolution of 0.2 seconds is coarse relative to millisecond-level human sensitivity cited in introduction (tens of ms)

Missing design justifications and sensitivity studies: batch size 30 for contrastive training (reducing hard negatives) explained post-hoc, no justification for frozen SigLIP 2 or specific frame rates (8/24 FPS), VAE fine-tuning relegated to appendix despite being important
Reproducibility concerns: missing sample link ('available at .'), no code/model release mentioned, some components (VideoPrism, SigLIP 2) may have access restrictions

strengths: Strong empirical results with clear improvements in synchronization (DeSync 0.497 vs MMAudio 0.521; Human MOS Sync 3.52 vs 2.92), demonstrating meaningful advances in key metrics

Novel first application of shortcut loss to video-to-audio generation domain, enabling high-quality few-step sampling (8 steps) without distillation or retraining, achieving practical near-real-time generation (0.71s for 10s audio)

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation including multiple objective metrics (FAD, KL divergence, IS, IB, DeSync), human listening studies with blind/randomized trials, ablation studies, and scaling experiments up to 1.01B parameters

Well-motivated technical contributions addressing real limitations: (1) contrastive synchronization learning with smaller batches to avoid semantic alignment problem, (2) masked flow matching for audio conditioning and spectral style transfer, (3) long-form generation via iterative outpainting

Excellent reproducibility with extensive implementation details, training hyperparameters, architectural specifications, and dataset descriptions; detailed appendix with algorithms and human evaluation protocol
Honest and transparent discussion of limitations, acknowledging unfairness in long-form comparisons and functional constraints of iterative outpainting approach, with practical suggested workarounds
Compact model size (643M parameters) outperforming larger models (MMAudio 1.03B, LoVA 1.06B), with consistent improvements across diverse metrics and long-form evaluation up to 30 seconds
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components are largely adaptations of concurrent work (shortcut loss from Frans et al. 2025, masked diffusion from Chen et al. 2025), with primary contribution being combination and application rather than fundamental innovation

Long-form generation relies on ad-hoc iterative outpainting with fixed 0.5-second prepend length, acknowledged to fail on scene cuts with different acoustic events; no quantitative analysis of failure frequency or when manual intervention is required

Evaluation fairness issues: long-form comparison with MMAudio explicitly noted by authors as unfair (different context windows), weakening claims about long-form superiority; should either compare under equal settings or separate claims more clearly
Synchronization metric (DeSync) has 0.2-second resolution, which is coarse given the intro emphasizes humans detect tens-of-milliseconds asynchrony; may miss fine-grained synchronization failures

Limited human evaluation scope: only 10 videos with 18 participants (180 scores total); no inter-rater reliability reported; selection criteria for videos not justified; combining orthogonal concepts (overall fit, sync, quality) in single MOS scale
Audio conditioning evaluation lacks human validation: only quantitative metrics (FAD, SWSD); no human study on perceptual quality of audio conditioning; limited failure case analysis

Insufficient ablations: no study of semantic feature resolution (8 FPS), synchronization resolution (24 FPS), or batching sensitivity; architectural choices (number of blocks, positions) appear arbitrary with no justification; shortcut loss consistency target ratio (25%) not ablated

Batch size selection for contrastive learning (28 maximum) is critical insight but lacks detailed ablation showing where performance saturates; relies on citation to Synchformer without independent verification
VAE fine-tuning approach (replacing first/last layers to increase frame rate from 21.5 to 43 Hz) appears crude with no ablation on its impact; why this modification was necessary not well explained
Missing comparisons with other audio conditioning approaches in V2A; parameter count varies widely across baselines (159M to 1.22B) making interpretability of comparisons difficult

strengths: Strong experimental validation with comprehensive metrics (FAD, DeSync, IS, human MOS across 18 participants, 10 videos) and ablations demonstrating superior synchronization (0.497 vs 0.521 DeSync) and human ratings (3.52 vs 2.92 on sync)
First application of shortcut loss in V2A enabling few-step sampling (8 steps) without quality degradation or post-hoc fine-tuning, while maintaining full-step performance

Well-designed masked flow matching approach enabling both audio conditioning for Foley/sound design and long-form generation via iterative outpainting, with novel SWSD metric for spectral preservation
Custom contrastive synchronization model using larger VideoPrism backbone addresses known failure modes better than prior Synchformer-based approaches
Comprehensive long-form evaluation up to 60 seconds with scaling study (1B parameters) showing consistent improvements, advancing beyond typical 8-12s V2A limitations
Clear presentation with good visualization of spectrograms, honest limitations discussion, and thorough appendix with implementation details and human evaluation methodology
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty—primarily applies existing techniques (flow matching, shortcut loss from Frans et al. 2025, masked objectives from Chen et al. 2025, standard contrastive learning) without significant methodological innovation

Long-form generation remains workaround-based despite framing: still requires iterative generation with reference prepending, doesn't solve stated 'unrestricted memory growth' problem, limited to ~10s context in practice, and only viable for single-scene videos without cuts

Long-form experimental setup potentially unfair—comparing against MMAudio (not designed for 30+ seconds) creates artificial advantage; hypothesis about unseen positional embeddings is speculative rather than empirically validated

Audio conditioning evaluation incomplete: only quantitative analysis on representative subset (Section A.3), SWSD metric novel but not validated against human perception, main evidence qualitative (Figures 5, 9), no human study specifically evaluating reference audio fidelity
Few-step generation not truly real-time (0.71s for 4 steps on A100) despite 'near-real-time' claims; only 4-step comparison shown with Frieren, 1-2 step performance only qualitative

Reproducibility concerns: multiple components require significant computation, no code/model release mentioned, project URL not provided, data filtering details insufficient, would require access to proprietary datasets

Synchronization model underspecified: trained only on VGGSound (generalization unclear), batch size sensitivity reasoning incomplete, no direct comparison vs. Synchformer, necessity vs. added complexity unclear, data filtering could introduce bias
Key design choices lack ablation: masking range (5ms-2.5s) unjustified, CFG 4.0 not explained, VAE 43Hz upgrade trade-offs not discussed, some hyperparameters (EMA 0.999) not justified

Experimental ambiguities: test set size/composition not clearly stated, human eval on only 10 videos is small, diversity unknown, baseline preprocessing consistency unclear, some baselines lack human eval numbers
Model size comparison confounded: SALSA-V 643M vs. MMAudio 1.03B complicates architecture assessment; baselines range 159M-1.22B; only 2 additional scaling points shown
